description.value: An fMRI study of brain responses to unisensory visual and multisensory visual-plus-odor smoking cues in nicotine-dependent adult cigarette smokers.

spans.text: the present study was designed to examine cue-reactivity in response to visual smoking cues in the presence and absence of a cigarette odor

value: We hypothesized greater drug cue reactivity to the combination of visual and odor drug cues than to the visual drug cues presented alone.

description.value: Smoking-related visual cue condition: blocks of five high-resolution cigarette-smoking-related advertisement or digital photographs, each displayed for approximately 4.8 seconds across a 24-second block. Participants passively viewed the images; no response demand was reported.

spans.text: non-smoking, neutral, images (NEU-I)

description.value: Neutral visual cue condition: blocks of five non-smoking, neutral high-resolution advertisement or digital photographs matched to the smoking pictures for intensity, color, and complexity, each displayed for approximately 4.8 seconds across a 24-second block. Participants passively viewed the images; no response demand was reported.

spans.text: propylene glycol (PG-O), the odorless control

description.value: Odorless control condition: propylene glycol delivered through the MRI-compatible olfactometer over the first 12 seconds of each 30-second block, paired with the visual cue block. Participants passively received the odorless control stimulus; no response demand was reported.

spans.text: freshly lit cigarette (CIG-O)

description.value: Cigarette-odor condition: freshly lit cigarette smoke odor delivered through the MRI-compatible olfactometer over the first 12 seconds of each 30-second block, paired with the visual cue block. Participants passively received the odor stimulus while viewing the images; no response demand was reported.

spans.text: Each run consisted of 18 pseudo-randomly interspersed 24-s blocks
